New task: make Wincheck easy for judges to try. Restart claude/gifted-cerf-lirfct from the latest origin/main.
1. MCP server: wincheck/mcp_server.py
Use the official mcp Python SDK (FastMCP).
Add it as an optional extra in pyproject.toml: [project.optional-dependencies] mcp = ["mcp>=1.2"].
Add a console script: wincheck-mcp = "wincheck.mcp_server:main". Keep mcp out of the core dependencies.
Tools (each runs sys.executable -m wincheck ... in a subprocess, so nothing prints to the MCP stdout; return the parsed JSON plus the exit code):
list_cases(): the 6 cases, with name, split (dev/held_out) and upstream repo@commit.
check_case(case): eval CASE --baseline-only. No model calls; it checks whether the bug reproduces on this machine.
run_case(case, effort="high", held_out=False): full agent run and score. Needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Pass --held-out only if held_out is true.
fix_issue(repo_path, issue_text, python_path=None): writes the issue to a temp file and runs wincheck run.
Use a long subprocess timeout (60 min), and return stderr's last 40 lines on failure.
Test it: start the server with the mcp stdio client in Python, list the tools, call list_cases, and call run_case without an API key to confirm it fails cleanly with exit code 2. Report the results.
2. README: add a "Try it yourself" section after Partner tools
Easiest, on GitHub's Windows runners: fork the repo → Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions → add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (and optionally NEATLOGS_API_KEY) → Actions tab → "wincheck" → Run workflow → pick a case and mode. Mention baseline mode needs no key.
On a Windows machine: pip install -e ., then python -m wincheck cases, python -m wincheck eval click-3277 --baseline-only, then python -m wincheck eval click-3277.
From Claude (MCP): pip install -e ".[mcp]", then the Claude Code command claude mcp add wincheck -- wincheck-mcp, and the matching Claude Desktop JSON config snippet. List the four tools in one line each.
Commit the two parts separately, with natural messages and no co-author trailer. Bundle only the new checkpoints (a bundle can hold several refs), scan them as before, push, open a PR, and don't merge. Reply with the PR link, the checkpoint IDs, the test results and the scan counts.

- session-start-hook (startup-hook-skill): Creating and developing startup hooks for Claude Code cloud sessions. Use when the user wants to set up a repository for cloud sessions, create a SessionStart hook to ensure their project can run tests and linters during cloud sessions.
- pdf-viewer:annotate: Collaboratively annotate a PDF — propose markup, review together, iterate
- pdf-viewer:fill-form: Fill PDF form fields interactively with live visual feedback
- pdf-viewer:open: Open a PDF in the interactive viewer
- pdf-viewer:sign: Place a signature or initials image on a PDF
- desktop-commander:ai-tools-setup: Set up, connect, validate, and repair Claude Desktop and MCP servers using Desktop Commander — inspecting and fixing mcp.json / claude_desktop_config.json, getting MCP servers to connect, and diagnosing local AI tooling. Use when a user wants to install, configure, connect, validate, or fix Claude Desktop, an MCP server, an MCP config file, or a local AI agent/gateway. Trigger on the symptoms that actually bring people in: "Claude can't see my tools", "my MCP server isn't showing up", "tools aren't loading in Claude", "add an MCP server", "my MCP isn't connecting", "fix my Claude Desktop config", "the agent won't respond", "wire up Ollama / LM Studio", "restart Claude Desktop". Also covers local agent gateways like OpenClaw and Hermes.
- desktop-commander:computer-health-check: Run a comprehensive, read-only health check on the user's computer and return a scored chat summary with prioritized, plain-English recommendations and safe cleanup suggestions. Use this whenever the user wants to check their computer's health, speed it up, free up / reclaim disk space, find what's eating CPU / memory / storage, check battery health and wear, audit login & startup items, see pending updates, or asks for a "tune-up", "checkup", "system report", "health check", or "is my Mac/PC/laptop healthy". Trigger even on casual phrasing like "my laptop feels slow", "why is my fan so loud", "my computer is laggy", "running out of space", or "clean up my machine". Works on macOS, Windows, and Linux. This is a Desktop Commander skill: it relies on a real local shell (start_process / interact_with_process) and is strictly read-only by default — it never needs sudo and only performs cleanups the user explicitly approves.
- desktop-commander:desktop-commander-overview: Use for Desktop Commander MCP capabilities — persistent shells and REPLs, long-running processes, filesystem beyond the workspace, structured files (.xlsx, .docx, .pdf, images) and large local data files such as CSVs, ripgrep search at scale, SSH, or cross-turn state.
- desktop-commander:knowledge-base: Create and maintain a Markdown knowledge base that any AI agent can read, search, and update. Use when the user wants to start a knowledge base, add or update notes, organize docs/notes for an agent or LLM to consume, build an index of notes, or run a cleanup/maintenance pass on an existing MD knowledge base. Triggers include "knowledge base", "KB", "notes for the agent", "index of notes", "second brain", "docs for AI context", "add a note", "update the KB".
- desktop-commander:obsidian-vault: Organize Obsidian vaults with MOCs, wikilinks, frontmatter/properties, dashboards, orphan-note checks, and cleanup workflows. Use ONLY when the user explicitly refers to Obsidian — by naming "Obsidian", an Obsidian "vault", or an Obsidian-specific feature such as wikilinks ("[[ ]]"), the Dataview or Bases plugins, or Obsidian Properties. Within that Obsidian context it covers creating Maps of Content, adding/fixing wikilinks, finding orphan notes, normalizing YAML frontmatter, generating Dataview/Bases dashboards, organizing folders, deduplicating or renaming notes, and preparing the vault for AI use. Do NOT use this skill for generic note-taking, Markdown, or knowledge-base requests that don't mention Obsidian.
- desktop-commander:terminal: Use Desktop Commander for terminal and command-line work, especially anything that needs a shell whose state persists across turns: Python/Node REPLs, database shells, dev servers and other long-running processes, SSH into remote machines, and Windows PowerShell. Also handles everyday terminal tasks — navigating folders, choosing the right command for the user's shell (PowerShell, cmd, bash, zsh), running Docker/curl/cloud-CLI commands, inspecting processes and ports, and saving recurring workflows as scripts — even when the user doesn't say "Desktop Commander" or "terminal." Reach for it on pasted errors like "command not found", "permission denied", "EADDRINUSE", "address already in use", "npm ERR!", "ModuleNotFoundError", or "ENOENT", and on intents like "what's using port 3000", "kill that process", "ssh into my server", or "why won't my dev server start". Works on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Never run destructive commands without explicit confirmation.

"""Command line entry point.

  wincheck run --repo PATH --issue-file ISSUE.md [--python VENV_PYTHON]
  wincheck eval CASE [--baseline-only] [--held-out]
  wincheck cases
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path

from . import tracing


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="wincheck")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    r = sub.add_parser("run", help="run the agent on a local checkout")
    r.add_argument("--repo", type=Path, required=True)
    r.add_argument("--issue-file", type=Path, required=True)
    r.add_argument("--python", default=sys.executable, help="python of the project's environment")
    r.add_argument("--runs", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    r.add_argument("--effort", default="high")

    e = sub.add_parser("eval", help="replay an upstream Windows bug and score the agent")
    e.add_argument("case")
    e.add_argument("--baseline-only", action="store_true", help="only check the case is valid on this machine")
    e.add_argument("--held-out", action="store_true", help="allow scoring a held-out case")
    e.add_argument("--runs", type=Path, default=Path("runs"))
    e.add_argument("--workdir", type=Path)
    e.add_argument("--issue-file", type=Path, help="use this issue text instead of fetching it from GitHub")
    e.add_argument("--effort", default="high")

    sub.add_parser("cases", help="list eval cases")
    args = ap.parse_args(argv)

    if args.cmd == "cases":
        from .evals import CASES
        for c in CASES.values():
            print(f"{c.name:22} {c.split:9} {c.repo}@{c.fix[:10]}")
        return 0

    if args.cmd != "eval" or not args.baseline_only:
        from .agent import api_key
        if not api_key():
            print("Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or WINCHECK_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    exporting = tracing.init(workflow_name="wincheck", tags=[args.cmd, getattr(args, "case", "local")])
    print(f"[wincheck] neatlogs export {'on' if exporting else 'off'}", flush=True)
    try:
        if args.cmd == "run":
            from .agent import Agent
            from .tools import Workspace
            env = os.environ.copy()
            env["PATH"] = str(Path(args.python).parent) + os.pathsep + env.get("PATH", "")
            ws = Workspace(args.repo, args.python, env)
            run_dir = args.runs / "local" / time.strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S")
            result = Agent(ws, args.issue_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), run_dir, effort=args.effort).run()
            print(json.dumps({k: v for k, v in result.__dict__.items() if k != "diff"}, indent=2))
            return 0 if result.status == "fixed" else 1

        from .evals import CASES, default_workdir, evaluate
        case = CASES.get(args.case)
        if case is None:
            print(f"unknown case {args.case}; see `wincheck cases`", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        if case.split == "held_out" and not args.held_out and not args.baseline_only:
            print(f"{case.name} is held out; pass --held-out to score it (once, at the end)", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        workdir = args.workdir or default_workdir()

+"""MCP server that exposes Wincheck to Claude and other MCP clients.

+

+
+import json

+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP
+

+STDERR_TAIL = 40
+
+mcp = FastMCP("wincheck")
+
+
+def _home() -> Path:
+    home = Path(os.environ.get("WINCHECK_HOME") or Path.home() / "wincheck")
+    home.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    return home
+
+

+    """The CLI prints log lines and then one indented JSON object; return that object."""
+    start = stdout.rfind("\n{\n")
+    start = 0 if stdout.startswith("{\n") else start + 1 if start >= 0 else -1
+    if start < 0:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return json.loads(stdout[start:])
+    except json.JSONDecodeError:
+        return None
+
+
+def _wincheck(*args: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "wincheck", *args]
+    try:

+        return {"exit_code": None, "error": f"timed out after {TIMEOUT // 60} minutes"}

+    if p.returncode != 0:
+        out["stderr_tail"] = "\n".join(p.stderr.splitlines()[-STDERR_TAIL:])
+    return out
+
+
+@mcp.tool()

+    """List the eval cases: name, split (dev or held_out) and upstream repo@commit."""

+    return _wincheck("eval", case, "--baseline-only")

# Wincheck

Wincheck is an agent that takes a Windows-specific bug report for a Python project, reproduces it on Windows, fixes it, and checks the fix. It won't change any code until it has a test that fails.

## How it works

The model drives each phase with tools. The harness controls when it moves to the next phase:

| Phase | What the model can do | Gate to the next phase |
|---|---|---|
| **read** | read files, list dirs, search | calls `start_reproduction` with a plan |
| **reproduce** | write **test files only**, run commands and tests | harness runs the submitted tests itself and every one must **fail** |
| **fix** | write **non-test files only** (tests are frozen) | harness runs the reproduction (must pass) and the whole test files it lives in (nothing that passed before may fail) |

If the bug doesn't reproduce, the agent calls `give_up` and makes no patch. If any test file changes during the fix phase, the harness restores it and rejects that attempt.

- Model: `claude-opus-5-5` through the Anthropic Python SDK, with a hand-written tool-use loop, adaptive thinking and streaming.
- Tracing: every run is a neatlogs `WORKFLOW` span. Each phase is an `AGENT` span, and each tool call and harness check is a `TOOL` span. The Anthropic calls are instrumented too.
- Secrets: API keys are removed from the environment of the project under test, so the model's commands can't read them.

## Evals

Each eval case is a real Windows bug that was fixed upstream. It is replayed from the commit before the fix (`<fix>^`). The agent sees only the issue text and that checkout. Two upstream fixes close no issue (`tox-str-convert`, `build-env`), so their issue text is a short symptom-only report in `wincheck/issues/`, and `score.json` records `issue_source: written`. Scoring uses the maintainers' own test from the fix commit: the target tests must fail before the agent runs and pass after it, and no other test in those files may start failing.

```
python -m wincheck cases
python -m wincheck eval click-3277 --baseline-only   # is the case valid on this machine? (no model calls)
python -m wincheck eval click-3277                   # run and score the agent
python -m wincheck run --repo PATH --issue-file ISSUE.md --python PATH\to\venv\python.exe
```

Each run writes `runs/<case>/<time>/` with `issue.md`, `baseline.json`, `transcript.jsonl`, `fix.patch`, `result.json` and `score.json`.

## Results

Latest agent run for each case on `windows-latest`. Every run, with links to its Actions log, is in [docs/evidence.md](docs/evidence.md).

| Case | Held out | Result |
|---|---|---|
| click-3277 | no | passed |
| tox-3222 | no | failed: 1 of 6 targets (kept an escape rule upstream changed) |
| click-tempfile-pager | yes | passed |
| pytest-pathlib | yes | passed (66 s, 9 turns) |
| build-env | yes | passed (347 s) |
| tox-str-convert | yes | failed: 18 of 20 targets, 2 regressions |

4 of 6 cases pass, including 3 of the 4 held-out ones.

## Partner tools

- **neatlogs**: every run is one trace. The run is a workflow span, each phase an agent span, and each tool call and harness check a tool span. The Anthropic calls are instrumented too. Runs are listed in [docs/evidence.md](docs/evidence.md).

  ![One Wincheck eval run in neatlogs: setup, baseline, the agent's read, reproduce and fix phases with every Claude and tool call, then the score](docs/images/neatlogs-trace.jpg)
- **Entire**: commits carry `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers. The first public checkpoint is [`01M4MT8VXPQRMM5SF9FWS0H8XE`](https://entire.io/gh/nftkingiii/wincheck/session/06c56b38-4221-5994-b5c1-a8a55c86ae0a). Cloud sessions can't push `refs/entire/*`, so [`entire-import.yml`](.github/workflows/entire-import.yml) publishes checkpoints from a git bundle.
- **cfo.ai**: a 12-month plan built from measured run costs. $49 per fix and a $199/month team plan both clear a 70% margin, and 23 paying repos cover founder pay. See the [summary PDF](docs/business/wincheck-financial-plan.pdf) and the [workbook](docs/business/wincheck-12-month-plan.xlsx).

 - **cfo.ai**: a 12-month plan built from measured run costs. $49 per fix and a $199/month team plan both clear a 70% margin, and 23 paying repos cover founder pay. See the [summary PDF](docs/business/wincheck-financial-plan.pdf) and the [workbook](docs/business/wincheck-12-month-plan.xlsx).
 
+## Try it yourself
+
+**Easiest: on GitHub's Windows runners**
+
+1. Fork this repo.
+2. In your fork, go to Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions and add `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (and optionally `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`).
+3. Open the Actions tab (enable workflows if GitHub asks), pick "wincheck" and click Run workflow.
+4. Pick a case and a mode. `baseline` only checks that the bug reproduces on Windows and needs no API key; `agent` runs and scores the agent. Held-out cases also need the "held out" box ticked.
+
+**On a Windows machine**
+
+```
+pip install -e .
+python -m wincheck cases
+python -m wincheck eval click-3277 --baseline-only   # no API key needed
+python -m wincheck eval click-3277                   # needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
+```
+
+**From Claude (MCP)**
+
+```
+pip install -e ".[mcp]"
+claude mcp add wincheck -- wincheck-mcp
+```
+
+For Claude Desktop, add this to `claude_desktop_config.json` (use the full path to `wincheck-mcp` if it isn't on your PATH):
+
+```json
+{
+  "mcpServers": {
+    "wincheck": {
+      "command": "wincheck-mcp",
+      "env": { "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "sk-ant-..." }
+    }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Runs are written under `WINCHECK_HOME` (default `~/wincheck`). The tools:
+
+- `list_cases`: the six cases, with split (dev or held_out) and upstream repo@commit.
+- `check_case(case)`: checks that the bug reproduces on this machine. No model calls.
+- `run_case(case, effort="high", held_out=False)`: runs the agent and scores it. Needs `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`.
+- `fix_issue(repo_path, issue_text, python_path=None)`: runs the agent on your own checkout and bug report.
+
 ## Windows runner
 
 The runs happen on GitHub Actions `windows-latest` (`.github/workflows/wincheck.yml`). The workflow can only be started by hand. Its API keys come from repository secrets (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `NEATLOGS_API_KEY`), and the run directory is uploaded as an artifact.

        tot["REDACTED_EMAIL markers"]+=d.count("REDACTED_EMAIL")
        for m in em.finditer(d):
            e=m.group(0).lower()

        for m in ph.finditer(d):
            s=m.group(0)
            if s.isdigit() and s in repo: tot["phone-like: public run ID"]+=1
            elif s in known: tot["phone-like: "+known[s]]+=1
            elif s.isdigit() and len(s)==13 and s.startswith("17"): tot["phone-like: ms timestamp"]+=1

EOF

input.body:
Makes Wincheck easy for judges to try.

**MCP server** (`wincheck/mcp_server.py`, `wincheck-mcp`): a FastMCP stdio server with four tools, `list_cases`, `check_case`, `run_case` and `fix_issue`. Each tool runs `python -m wincheck ...` in a subprocess (60-minute timeout), so nothing prints to the MCP stdout. It returns the parsed JSON and exit code, plus the last 40 lines of stderr on failure. `mcp` is an optional extra (`pip install -e ".[mcp]"`) and stays out of the core dependencies. It is pinned to `mcp>=1.2,<2` because mcp 2.x removed `mcp.server.fastmcp`.

Tested with the mcp stdio client (Linux, no API key):
- the server lists 4 tools
- `list_cases` returns all 6 cases with split and upstream repo@commit (exit 0)
- `run_case("click-3277")` fails cleanly with exit code 2 and "Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY…" in stderr_tail
- an unknown case returns exit code 2 with the CLI's error

**README**: a "Try it yourself" section after Partner tools, covering the Actions workflow on a fork (baseline mode needs no key), a local Windows machine, and the MCP server from Claude Code or Claude Desktop.

The third commit adds `entire-checkpoints.bundle` with the two checkpoint refs for `entire-import.yml`. It was scanned for emails, phone numbers, keys and personal details. Remove it before squash-merging.

The MCP server and the "Try it yourself" README section are up for review in https://github.com/nftkingiii/wincheck/pull/16. I haven't merged it.

**One change from your spec:** the extra is `mcp = ["mcp>=1.2,<2"]`, not `mcp>=1.2`. With your pin, pip installed mcp 2.3.0, which no longer has FastMCP (it was renamed `MCPServer`), and the server crashed on start. Pinning below 2 installs 1.30.0 and keeps FastMCP. `mcp` stays out of the core dependencies.

**Commits:**
1. `43c9752`: MCP server, the optional extra and the `wincheck-mcp` command.
2. `f61b6fb`: the "Try it yourself" section, with the fork + Actions route, local Windows commands, and the Claude Code and Claude Desktop setup.
3. `8edfc2b`: only the bundle.

**Checkpoint IDs:**
- `01M4PDB1Y3B7EDXGJX5NYMC9HY` (MCP server)
- `01M4PDBKFPYB54GN93ZE6MKFWC` (README)

**Test results** (mcp stdio client, Linux, no API key):
- **Tools listed:** `list_cases`, `check_case`, `run_case`, `fix_issue`.
- **`list_cases`:** exit code 0, all 6 cases with split and repo@commit.
- **`run_case("click-3277")`:** fails cleanly with exit code 2 and "Set ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (or WINCHECK_ANTHROPIC_API_KEY)".
- **`run_case("pytest-pathlib")`:** also exit code 2, same message.
- **Unknown case:** exit code 2 with the error from the wincheck CLI.
- **Not tested:** `check_case` and `fix_issue` on a real case. They need a Windows machine and an API key.

**Two choices I made:**
- Runs are written under `WINCHECK_HOME` (default `~/wincheck`). Claude Desktop may start the server from a folder it can't write to, so I didn't use the current folder.
- `list_cases` reads the CLI's plain-text output, so commits are shown shortened to 10 characters.

I found one bug in mcp_server.py. neatlogs prints ... - neatlogs - INFO - Neatlogs SDK shutdown complete to stdout, right after the CLI's JSON. Apply the _last_json fix.

"Checkpoint 01M4PDBKFPYB54GN93ZE6MKFWC: Try it yourself section".

"""Run pytest in the target project's environment and read back per-test outcomes."""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import subprocess
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

# "PASSED tests/x.py::test_a" / "FAILED tests/x.py::test_b - AssertionError"
_SUMMARY = re.compile(r"^(PASSED|FAILED|ERROR|XFAIL|XPASS|SKIPPED)\s+(.+?)\s*$")


@dataclass
class PytestResult:
    returncode: int
    outcomes: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    output: str = ""
    timed_out: bool = False

    def outcome(self, test_id: str) -> str:
        """Outcome for a node id, or "MISSING" when pytest never reported it."""
        if test_id in self.outcomes:
            return self.outcomes[test_id]
        norm = normalize_id(test_id)
        for tid, out in self.outcomes.items():
            if normalize_id(tid) == norm:
                return out
        return "MISSING"


def normalize_id(test_id: str) -> str:
    path, sep, rest = test_id.partition("::")
    return path.replace("\\", "/") + sep + rest


def parse_summary(output: str) -> dict[str, str]:
    outcomes: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in output.splitlines():
        m = _SUMMARY.match(line)
        if not m:
            continue
        status, rest = m.groups()
        if status in ("FAILED", "ERROR") and " - " in rest:
            rest = rest.split(" - ", 1)[0]
        if status == "SKIPPED" or "::" not in rest:
            # skip lines look like "SKIPPED [1] path:line: reason"
            continue
        # an ERROR in teardown after a PASS should still count against the test
        if outcomes.get(rest) in ("FAILED", "ERROR"):
            continue
        outcomes[rest] = status
    return outcomes


def run_pytest(
    python: str,
    cwd: Path,
    args: list[str],
    timeout: int = 900,
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> PytestResult:
    cmd = [python, "-m", "pytest", "-rA", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", "--color=no", *args]
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            cwd=cwd,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            encoding="utf-8",
            errors="replace",
            timeout=timeout,
            env=env or os.environ.copy(),
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as exc:
        return PytestResult(returncode=-1, output=_text(exc.stdout) + _text(exc.stderr), timed_out=True)
    output = proc.stdout + ("\n" + proc.stderr if proc.stderr else "")
    return PytestResult(proc.returncode, parse_summary(output), output)


def _text(data: str | bytes | None) -> str:
    if data is None:
        return ""
    return data.decode("utf-8", "replace") if isinstance(data, bytes) else data


def clip(text: str, limit: int = 20000) -> str:
    """Keep the head and the tail; pytest puts the useful part at the end."""
    if len(text) <= limit:
        return text
    head = limit // 4
    tail = limit - head
    return f"{text[:head]}\n\n... [{len(text) - limit} chars cut] ...\n\n{text[-tail:]}"
